newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Japan to propose export bank cooperation at APEC.
newsitem.headline: Japan to propose export bank cooperation at APEC.

text.p: Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka will propose initiatives for cooperation among the region's export banks at the APEC finance ministers forum this weekend, a senior Ministry of Finance (MOF) official said on Friday.

Finance ministers of the 18-member APEC forum are meeting on the Philippine island of Cebu to forge proposals to promote stable and transparent financial markets in the region, boost private sector investment in developing Asian infrastructure, and discuss other economic issues, including current foreign exchange rates.

Export-related financial institutions in Asia finance about 40 percent of the region's infrastructure projects such as building power plants, and cooperation among them will increase their efficiency and lure more private sector investment, the official said.

Among the APEC (Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation) group members, Australia, Canada, China, South Korea, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, Thailand, Taiwan and the United States have export- related financial institutions, he said.
The Japan Export-Import Bank will initiate a meeting of those institutions within the APEC framework to exchange information and propose guidelines, he said.
The other APEC members are Indonesia, New Zealand, Chile, Brunei, Papua New Guinea, Hong Kong, Singapore and the Philippines.
Mitsuzuka will also meet finance ministers or officials of China, Taiwan, Thailand, South Korea and the Philippines, as well as Philippine President Fidel Ramos.

Mitsuzuka has already met with U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin on Friday in Tokyo ahead of the APEC meeting, and there are no plans for the two to meet again separately in Cebu, the official said.
